q8.answer: Counts live in one shared managed Redis, as a key per customer per window, rl:{customerId}:{windowStart}, so all 6 gateways read and write the same number. Old counters are removed by EXPIRE 120, set when the key is created; it is only cleanup.

q9.answer: Budget resets when the fixed one-minute window rolls over. The next minute uses a new key, so the count starts at zero. There is no sliding window or refund; rejected requests do not use up budget, and a backend failure does not refund the count.

q10.answer: The check and increment run as one atomic Lua script in Redis. Redis runs scripts one at a time, so two gateways cannot both take the last slot. The script reads the count, rejects if count >= limit, otherwise increments.

q11.answer: The script computes it from Redis TIME only: seconds left in the window, windowStart + 60 - time, rounded up and at least 1. The gateway clock is not used, so drift does not matter.

q12.answer: No retry in v1, and no local counter or circuit breaker. The gateway waits up to 50 ms, emits ratelimit_store_unavailable, and forwards the request. The client gets no X-RateLimit-* headers on that response, because the values are unknown.
